dedupe_keys.name: usda nass cold storage survey and capacity of refrigerated warehouses

description: The Cold Storage survey measures the stocks of perishable food held in refrigerated warehouses across the United States at the end of each month: butter and cheeses, pork and pork bellies, beef, chicken and turkey, frozen fruits, berries, vegetables, potatoes and orange juice. A companion biennial survey of refrigerated warehouse capacity updates the list of facilities and their space. The producer is the National Agricultural Statistics Service of the U.S. Department of Agriculture, which surveys about 600 firms by mail and 200 more by e-mail, covering about 78 percent of national storage capacity, and imputes non-respondents. Coverage is national and regional, monthly, with an annual summary each February and long historical series. Reports and data are free through NASS publications and the Quick Stats database and API; no licence is stated, as a federal work. Caveats: only facilities storing targeted products for 30 days or more are listed, figures are revised the following month, and the survey gives stocks, not facility locations or temperatures. Simulation uses: buffer stock levels in food supply chain resilience models, capacity of the cold chain as a constraint in disruption and power outage scenarios, and seasonal inventory baselines. Related records: FAOSTAT food balances (data-faostat) give annual national supply.
